068051271a: User Interface: Wallet, Console, Command Line and API of Genoryn Krypton
084fe00fdd: One wallet for people. One API for programs.
33bfa7c3de: Most people will only ever see the desktop wallet: a window with a balance, a Send button and a Start mining button. Under it is the same node and the same commands that a server or an exchange uses. Pick the one that fits what you are doing.
9a24a1799d: The wallet is a small program that runs entirely on your computer and shows itself in its own window. Keys are made there and never leave; proofs are built there; what nodes tell it is checked there.
34022fd7c5: <0>Wallet.</0> Any number of wallets, each with its own 24 words and password. Balance, private payments with an optional memo, your address and its QR code to be paid with, in full or in a short form.
c48fcafaa1: <0>History.</0> Every payment, with search and filters, a <1>Proof</1> button to prove a payment to someone, and a link that opens its transaction or block on the explorer.
58cb78cbe5: <0>Swap.</0> Buy or sell GNR for bitcoin, wallet to wallet, with no exchange and no custody. Offers can follow the market price by themselves, within a limit you set.
bb5afe18a2: <0>Mining.</0> Choose a graphics card or the processor and press Start. It shows your share of the network and what it earns.
3e4d2040a3: <0>Network.</0> Live charts, peers, and the switch between light mode and your own full node.
7c24cd1138: <0>Console.</0> Ask the chain and the wallet by command. More on it below.
94369bff09: <0>Security and About.</0> Passwords, locks, the recovery phrase, updates.
22f7dc7879: Dark and light themes, and updates that are checked against the project's post-quantum signature before they install.
4c22a9b4a4: The wallet has a console, as Bitcoin's has: a line to type commands on, with their answers above it. Start typing and it offers the commands that match; <0>Tab</0> completes one, the arrow keys bring back earlier lines, and <1/> lists them all.
469828716f: Since 1.0.52 it looks and feels like a terminal: its top bar names the node it asks and says that it only reads, the commands people use most are one click away above the prompt, and every command and answer is set apart so a long session stays easy to read.
5f78396726: <0>The console only reads.</0> No command can send GNR, show a recovery phrase or a key, or change a setting. That is deliberate. In other wallets, people have been talked into pasting a command that handed over their coins; here there is no such command. Nobody ever needs you to type anything into the console to "verify" or "repair" a wallet.
c5bbb7d2d0: Questions about the chain go to the node your wallet uses, your own if you run one. A transaction's amount and parties stay hidden there as everywhere.
acea66eaed: is the same wallet without a window. It verifies what a node tells it exactly as the desktop wallet does.
165fe858d8: is the full node, and <0/> the miner. Each explains itself with <1/>. See the <2>full-node guide</2> and <3>Mining</3>.
78e5e49f11: Every node answers on this computer, port 30334, in three ways. None of them can spend anything: a node holds no keys.
00fb317e27: Plain addresses that answer JSON: <0/>, <1/>, <2/>, <3/>, <4/>, and more for wallets, miners and the swap board.

6db6e77bd3: At <0/>: a message for every new block and every new transaction, as they arrive.
aedb1e159a: The public node at genoryn.io answers the same questions, with limits per visitor. There are SDKs for TypeScript and JavaScript, for Rust and for C. The whole reference, with what an exchange needs to list GNR, is in the <0>documentation</0>.
